# Choosing a filter

One page over the fourteen free filters, drawn from each pack's own guide: what each is for, how long it holds up, and where it fails. Choose here, then read the chosen pack's guide in full (`read_pack`) before placing or tuning it: its values are the ones to use.

## How to choose

1. **Start from the moment, not the filter.** Find the moment in the film that calls for a look (a headline that should feel published, a memory, the problem before the product, a hit on the beat) and the filter whose moments below match it. No moment calls for one: use none.
2. **Keep to its length.** Most filters are an accent of a few seconds over the moment that calls for them, between clean shots. With no span named, lay it over that moment only, as long as its How long says, and say where you put it. Only a light finish may run the whole film unasked.
3. **Check the picture against Fails on.** A dark shot, an interface, numbers or small type under a strong filter: use the guide's mending setting, move the words to a track above the filter clip, or choose another filter.
4. **Stack by role.** Colour goes lowest, a medium (`crt`, `vhs`) just under the finish, a finish (`grain`, `paper`) on top; each Role below says where it goes and what doesn't go with it (`paper` never with a print filter, nothing over `dither`).

## Print

| Filter | Role | Moments it is for | How long | Fails on |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `emile/cmyk` CMYK | Structure: it remakes the picture as print, keeping its colours. A finish may go over it. | Blown up from an ad · A comic beat · "In print everywhere" | An accent: 1–3 seconds, the moment something is "in print". Never a long stretch, never over a shot whose information must be read. | Dark pictures: the worst case of all the filters here, almost nothing of a low-key portrait is left. · A white page of interface: the screen has little to print and chews the small text. · Text under 40 px, and coloured text of any size. |
| `emile/halftone` Halftone | Structure: it remakes the picture. Colour under it is lost; a finish (grain) may go over it. | A statement that should feel published · A poster beat · The past | An accent: one moment of 1–4 seconds (a line, a poster held still), five seconds at most for a section. Never over a shot whose information must be read (an interface, numbers, body text). | Dark pictures: most of the frame prints solid and the subject is lost (a low-key portrait, a night set). · Text in a mid-tone or a colour, and any text under 32 px: it breaks into dots. · More than about five seconds at a time: it tires the eye. |
| `emile/risograph` Risograph | Structure: it remakes the picture in two inks. Nothing goes under it but the picture; a finish is not needed (it brings its own sand and paper). | An independent or creative brand introducing itself · A friendly "how it works" · Chapter cards and the end card | Mostly an accent: a title card, a chapter card, the end card, 2–5 seconds. A whole opening (about ten seconds) only when the brand itself is independent and hand-made. | Dark pictures: two inks overprinted only reach a dark plum, so a low-key frame turns to one murky field (checked on a low-key portrait; no setting mends it). · A picture all in one hue (a blue lake printed in blue and red is just blue). · Colours that must be exact (a brand colour, a product's colour): every colour becomes a mix of the two inks. |

## Texture

| Filter | Role | Moments it is for | How long | Fails on |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `emile/dither` Dither | Structure: it remakes the picture in two colours. Nothing over it: a finish would blur the pixels. | Under the hood · The machine's view · A stencil or a photocopy | An accent: 1–4 seconds, the moment we see as the machine does; it only works between clean shots. Never a long stretch. | Low-key pictures: the darks fall into solid ink (a low-key portrait keeps little). · Text in a mid-tone, and small text. · Fast or textured motion: the pattern stays still while the picture moves under it, and it crawls. · Long stretches. |
| `emile/grain` Grain | Finish: the last filter on top, over colour and structure. | People and feeling · Night and mood · One film from many sources | A finish, so it may run long: at amount 0.25 or under it can cover the whole film and give footage from different sources one surface. Heavier (0.4 and up) only for one moody section. | Small text and fine interface at amount above 0.3: the grain sits in the letters. · Footage that is already noisy. · A bright, crisp, high-tech look. |
| `emile/paper` Paper | Finish: on top, over colour. Not with halftone, risograph or cmyk: they bring their own paper. | A storybook explainer · Words on a page · Heritage and craft | A finish, so it may run long: an illustrated explainer or words on a page can take it for a section or the whole film (texture 0.5 or under). Never on live footage or product shots. | Dark scenes: the sheet can't be seen under dark ink, and the blacks only go grey. · Photographs and footage meant to look real: the tooth reads as dirt on the lens. |

## Distort

| Filter | Role | Moments it is for | How long | Fails on |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `emile/displace` Displace | Optics: over the picture and its colour, under a finish. | The problem · A hit on the music · A breach, a failure, a system out of control · A still poster | An accent: 0.3–1.5 seconds, on the beat or the moment something goes wrong. Past two seconds it means nothing. | Long spans: it tires and stops meaning anything. · Calm, trust and reassurance (money, health, safety). · Words that must be read during the hit: a slipped band cuts through letters. |
| `emile/fluted-glass` Fluted glass | Optics: over the picture and its colour, under a finish. A filter clip changes every track under it, so type that must be read goes on a track above the clip. | Before the reveal · A ground for a headline · Privacy and trust | An accent: 1–3 seconds before a reveal, or a ground for one line of large type. Never over information that must be read; words go on a track above the filter. | Anything that must be read: letters double behind the ribs (a product's screen turns unreadable). · Thin lines and small interface: they break up. |

## Color

| Filter | Role | Moments it is for | How long | Fails on |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `emile/duotone` Duotone | Colour: under structure and finish. | Many sources, one brand · Memory · Emphasis · A ground for type | A section: one shot to one scene (a memory, an emphasis, a ground for words). The whole film only to pull mixed sources into the brand's two colours, and only when asked. | Pictures where colour carries meaning: a chart with coloured series, a product in several colours, red and green for bad and good. · A whole long film: the eye stops seeing it. |
| `emile/palette` Palette | Colour that also simplifies shape: under structure and finish. | `poster` (ink, maroon, vermilion, ochre, paper) · `thermal` (indigo to white-hot), soft 0.8–1 · `cyanotype` (blues of a blueprint) · `moss` (greens to bone) · `silver` (five greys of a darkroom print) · `primary` (black, blue, red, yellow, paper) | An accent: 2–5 seconds, one designed moment; thermal can carry a whole shot about seeing what is hidden. Never the whole film. | Dark pictures at the defaults: everything falls into the darkest ink (a low-key portrait, a night set). · Noisy footage: the edges speckle. · Colours that must be exact. |

## Glow

| Filter | Role | Moments it is for | How long | Fails on |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `emile/bloom` Bloom | Optics: over the picture and its colour, under a finish. Grain over it suits it. | Night and dark-mode heroes · Switching on · A dream or a memory | As long as the shot: the dark shot with points of light, for its whole length. It is restrained and hides nothing. | Bright pictures: nothing happens (checked: a bright product set and a white page of interface come out unchanged). · A wide, soft glow that fills the frame: the radius stops at about 2% of the frame's short side, because a filter draws in one pass. · Fine detail one or two pixels wide looked at closely: its glow is a little uneven. |

## Film

| Filter | Role | Moments it is for | How long | Fails on |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `emile/chromatic-aberration` Chromatic aberration | Optics: over the picture and its colour, under a finish. | To make a clean picture feel photographed · A moment of overload | lens at a low strength may follow a whole shot, or the whole film, to give rendered pictures a lens. shift is a hit of 0.3–1 second only. | shift over words that must be read: letters triple. · shift for a whole scene: it stops being a moment. · lens at high strength on an interface with small text near the corners. |
| `emile/crt` CRT | Medium: the last thing before a finish; it shows whatever is under it on a tube. | Then and now · A feed · Games and early computing | A section: the "back then" part, 2–6 seconds, or one screen inside the frame. Never the whole film. | Small text: 24 px type softens between the lines. · Fine detail that must stay crisp (a product beauty shot). · Films that will be watched very small: the phosphor stripes can shimmer when the player scales them. |
| `emile/vhs` VHS | Medium: the last thing before a finish; it shows whatever is under it as a tape. | A memory on tape · Found footage and behind the scenes · Nostalgia on purpose · The old way | A section: the memory or the old footage, 2–6 seconds, then a cut back to the clean present. The whole film only when the whole film is about the past. | Small text: everything softens sideways, body text under 28 px blurs. · A crisp interface demo or a product beauty shot. · The whole of a film that isn't about the past. |

## Words people use

- `emile/cmyk`: CMYK, four-colour, offset print, comic, pulp, billboard, catalogue, misprint
- `emile/halftone`: print, newspaper, editorial, zine, poster, manifesto, archive, punk
- `emile/risograph`: riso, risograph, zine, two-colour print, print shop, indie, craft, hand-made, playful
- `emile/dither`: dither, 1-bit, bitmap, pixel, early Macintosh, e-ink, terminal, stencil, photocopy, xerox
- `emile/grain`: grain, film grain, 16 mm, texture, analogue, organic, cinematic
- `emile/paper`: paper, sheet, letterpress, watercolour paper, tactile, matte, storybook, stationery
- `emile/displace`: glitch, slice, slip, displaced, corrupted, broken signal, jitter, tension, impact
- `emile/fluted-glass`: fluted glass, reeded glass, ribbed glass, frosted, behind glass, refraction, privacy
- `emile/duotone`: duotone, two-colour, two-tone, monochrome, tinted, toned, in brand colours
- `emile/palette`: posterize, screen print, limited palette, gradient map, thermal, heat map, infrared, blueprint, cyanotype
- `emile/bloom`: bloom, glow, halation, light bleed, soft light, luminous, night
- `emile/chromatic-aberration`: chromatic aberration, lens fringe, colour fringing, RGB split, prism, dispersion
- `emile/crt`: CRT, tube television, old monitor, scan lines, arcade, nineties, terminal, surveillance, broadcast
- `emile/vhs`: VHS, tape, camcorder, home video, analogue, tracking, rewind, lo-fi, nostalgia
